chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Do I prostrate upon the asphalt, meaning the bitumen/pitch?' He said, 'No, and not upon the cloth, nor the cotton pads, nor upon the wool, nor upon anything from the animals, nor upon food, nor upon anything from the fruits of the earth, nor upon anything from the feathers.'

key_terms.زِيفْت: Asphalt or bitumen, a synthetic or petroleum-based material
key_terms.قِير: Pitch or bitumen, often used interchangeably with zift in this context
key_terms.كُرْسُف: Cotton pads or thin cotton cloth

ai.seo_question: What materials are prohibited for prostration during Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) delineates the invalidating materials for *sajdah* by categorizing them into distinct groups: bitumen, textiles, animal derivatives, and organic produce. This classification reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *taharah* (purity) and *khushu* (humility), ensuring the worshipper prostrates on a clean, stable, and non-distracting surface that does not contain impurities or edible elements, thereby preserving the sanctity of the prayer posture.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to himasws, ‘Can I perform Sajdah upon the asphalt, meaning the synthetic fabric (plastic/petroleum based)?’. So heasws said: ‘No, and neither upon the cloth, nor the cotton pads, nor upon the wool, nor upon anything from the animals, nor upon food, nor upon anything from the fruits of the earth, nor upon anything from the feathers’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can I perform Sajdah (prostration) on asphalt? He (the Imam) said, ‘No, also not on cotton, wool, anything from animals, food, fruits of earth and not on anything of clothing.’”
